summary: The note outlines twelve strategies for funding local community theater productions in the post-pandemic period, each illustrated with an example theater group and dated initiatives since September 1, 2023. Strategies include business sponsorships, membership tiers, crowdfunding, galas, workshops, grants, alumni networks, subscriptions, social media, named seats, and media relations. The note concludes that combining these tactics helps theaters sustain themselves and thrive.
one_line: Twelve example-backed strategies, from sponsorships and crowdfunding to galas and named seats, for funding local community theater productions.
key_facts: James McCarter, director of the Springfield Community Playhouse, started a "Spotlight on Business" program in October 2023 offering local businesses advertising in playbills, lobbies, and naming opportunities.
Laura Edmonds, chairperson of the Rivertown Actors Guild, implemented a tiered patron system on January 10, 2024, offering acknowledgment in programs and VIP seating.

The Oceanview Theater Collective raised over $15,000 through a Kickstarter campaign in November 2023 for a holiday-themed production, offering virtual meet-and-greets, signed memorabilia, and cameo roles.

Melanie Charleson, a board member of the City Lights Community Theater, championed the "Masquerade Under the Stars" gala on December 15, 2023, which sold out and raised over $25,000 through auctions, raffles, and a catered dinner.
In August 2024 the Downtown Theater Alliance invited theatrical coach Roberta Keen to conduct acting workshops, which produced a steady income stream that helped subsidize productions.
Richard Tate, grant manager of the Midtown Arts Foundation, diversified grant applications and won three grants totaling $50,000 for the "Theatre in the Park" initiative in early 2024.
The Lakeside Players launched an "Alumni Spotlight Series" in May 2024 where past members shared career successes, encouraging donations and mentorship.

Annie Rodriguez, box office manager of the Starlight Theatre Collective, started a flexible subscription service in February 2024 with discounts and priority seating, increasing advance sales and revenue predictability.
The Hillcrest Community Theatre ran behind-the-scenes and live Q&A sessions on Instagram, increasing ticket sales and website donation traffic.
The Bright Horizons Playhouse created a "Take a Seat" campaign in September 2023 with named plaques on seats, leading to a fully funded renovation of its seating area.
Journalist Olivia Spencer covered the opening night of the Main Street Playhouse's fundraising season on her arts blog, boosting ticket sales and donations.
